questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Use ratios to compare quantities and solve proportional problems.
questions.prompt: Share 72 seedlings between two classes in the ratio 5:4. How many does the class with the larger share receive?
questions.explanation: There are 9 equal shares of 8 seedlings. The larger class share is 5 × 8.

verification.purpose: Check the calculation used in the worked answer.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Use ratios to compare quantities and solve proportional problems.
questions.prompt: Mix A uses 2 cups of concentrate for 5 cups of water. Mix B uses 3 cups of concentrate for 8 cups of water. Which has more concentrate per cup of water?
options: Mix B
Both have the same amount per cup of water
Mix A
It cannot be determined without knowing the cup size
questions.explanation: 2/5 = 16/40 and 3/8 = 15/40. Mix A has the higher concentrate-to-water ratio.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Use ratios to compare quantities and solve proportional problems.
questions.prompt: A printer uses 18 sheets to make 6 identical booklets. How many sheets are needed for 11 booklets?
questions.explanation: There are 3 sheets per booklet, so 11 booklets use 33 sheets.

verification.purpose: Check the calculation used in the worked answer.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Use ratios to compare quantities and solve proportional problems.
questions.prompt: At a stall, 4 oranges cost ₦600 and 6 cost ₦840. Which pack costs less per orange, and by how much?

The 4-pack, by ₦10 per orange
The 6-pack, by ₦40 per orange
Both cost the same per orange
questions.explanation: The two unit prices are ₦150 and ₦140.

verification.purpose: Check the calculation used in the worked answer.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.subtopic: Part of a whole and change
questions.learningObjective: Interpret percentages and calculate simple percentage changes.
questions.prompt: A school has 25 pupils in Group A and 50 in Group B. Exactly 20% of each group brings lunch. Which conclusion is correct?
questions.answer: Group B has twice as many pupils who bring lunch.
options: Group B has twice as many pupils who bring lunch.
Both groups have the same number bringing lunch.
Group A has twice as many pupils who bring lunch.
Group B has 20 more pupils who bring lunch.
questions.explanation: Five pupils in A and ten in B bring lunch. The percentages are equal, but the groups have different sizes.
